reviews.body: The new cases fix ordinary numeric ordering. Two boundary regressions remain: finite `float` and `decimal` overrides can disagree with their JSON values at a threshold, and nonfinite `float` overrides can incorrectly match numeric rules. AI-assisted review.

Thanks for the updates — both the JSON-value boundary handling and the non-finite guards resolve cleanly on `net8.0` and address the earlier threads (`#discussion_r4637582491` and `#discussion_r4637582499`) on modern .NET. Two `netstandard2.0` / `.NET Framework` compatibility issues remain before approval: `float.IsFinite`/`double.IsFinite` breaks `netstandard2.0` compilation, and default `float.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` truncates 8–9 digit floats to `G7` on `.NET Framework 4.x`. AI-assisted review.

Looks great — thanks for fixing the `netstandard2.0` finiteness check, switching `float` formatting to `"R"`, and adding the 8-digit float test cases. Verified multi-target `netstandard2.0`/`netstandard2.1`/`net8.0` Release builds, `PostHog` packaging, formatting, and the `net8.0` unit test suite locally. AI-assisted review.

review_comments.body:
### [P1] IMPORTANT — Compare finite `float` and `decimal` overrides using their JSON numeric value

**Introduced · REQUIRED · `src/PostHog/Json/PropertyFilterValue.cs:890–891`, RIGHT**

A locally evaluated `score > "0.1"` rule now enables the flag for `PersonProperties = new() { ["score"] = 0.1f }`. It should not match: the SDK sends the same value as JSON `0.1`. The inclusive rule `score <= "0.1"` flips the other way and no longer matches.

The merge base’s lexical fallback happened to give the correct result at this boundary. The new cast widens `0.1f` to `0.10000000149011612`, whereas parsing the emitted JSON `0.1` produces the same binary64 value as the condition. The decimal arm has a related issue: on .NET 9.0.8 the SDK emits `1.0000000000000003` for `1.0000000000000003m`, which parses as `1.0000000000000002`, but the direct cast produced `1.0000000000000004`. The [numeric criteria contract](https://github.com/PostHog/sdk-specs/blob/b0ea111a247b1b2b71d33690d3da7ce08282ad4a/openspec/specs/local-feature-flag-evaluator/spec.md#L778-L784) compares the supplied JSON number as binary64, not the original CLR representation.

| Executed comparator case | Merge base → head | Expected and parsed-wire control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0.1f`, `gt "0.1"` | false → true | false |
| `0.1f`, `lte "0.1"` | true → false | true |
| `1.0000000000000003m`, `lt "1.0000000000000004"` | true → false | true |
| Next `float` above `0.1f`, `gt "0.1"` | true → true | true |

A secret-key client calling `EvaluateFlagsAsync` with a loaded, active single-rule flag and the boxed property reaches these arms through `LocalEvaluator.MatchProperty`. Group overrides reach the same code. A resolved local result can change application branching and recorded exposure. The `float` case needs only a common fractional threshold; the decimal case does not imply that typical two-decimal prices fail.

Consider converting the finite `float` and `decimal` values from representations that round the same way as the SDK’s emitted JSON numbers, then comparing as binary64. Add the table rows to `LocalFeatureFlagsLoaderTests.VersionedDefinitionSnapshots`: use `DefinitionsJson` to load a single-rule flag, supply the boxed override through `EvaluateFlagsAsync`, and assert the flag is present, resolved to the expected value, and produced no `/flags` request. Keep the adjacent-`float` control so a fix cannot pass by rounding genuinely larger values down. The comparator and serializer cases above ran; this public-entry test is an unexecuted sketch.

### [P1] IMPORTANT — Do not let nonfinite `float` overrides satisfy numeric rules

**Introduced for the demonstrated cases · REQUIRED · `src/PostHog/Json/PropertyFilterValue.cs:890`, RIGHT**

A locally evaluated `score < "0"` rule now enables the flag when a calculation supplies `PersonProperties = new() { ["score"] = float.NaN }`. Likewise, `float.NegativeInfinity` newly matches `score < "-1"`. Both should definitively fail the rule. These are valid CLR inputs to the public override dictionary; no malformed JSON or transport failure is needed.

The base’s lexical fallback did not match either example. The new cast feeds [`Double.CompareTo`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.double.compareto?view=net-9.0), whose sort order places NaN and negative infinity below finite values. `LocalEvaluator.MatchProperty` turns that ordering into a true `lt`. The [numeric criteria contract](https://github.com/PostHog/sdk-specs/blob/b0ea111a247b1b2b71d33690d3da7ce08282ad4a/openspec/specs/local-feature-flag-evaluator/spec.md#L778-L784) requires a definite no-match. The probe also confirmed that the SDK serializes the NaN override as `{"person_properties":{"score":null}}`; the converter does the same for infinities. A null reaching the backend numeric matcher does not satisfy the comparison.

| Executed comparator case | Merge base → head | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `float.NaN`, `lt "0"` | false → true | false |
| `float.NegativeInfinity`, `lt "-1"` | false → true | false |
| `-1f`, `lt "0"` | true → true | true |

`+Infinity > "-1"` and `-Infinity < "1"` were already incorrectly true on base. The two new matches above resolve locally and can change targeting or exposure without a request to correct the result.

Consider returning a definitive no-match for nonfinite properties with valid numeric conditions in the flag-ordering path. Merely skipping the new cast arm still permits lexical fallback. Add the table rows to the same single-rule `EvaluateFlagsAsync` fixture: assert that both invalid rows are present and disabled, with no unresolved reason or `/flags` request, and that the finite control is enabled. A shared guard should cover NaN and both infinities across all four operators. The comparator cases ran; the public-entry sketch did not.

**Breaking:** `LocalEvaluator.IsFinite` calls `float.IsFinite` and `double.IsFinite`, which do not exist in `netstandard2.0` and break `PostHog` compilation and NuGet packaging.

`src/PostHog/PostHog.csproj:5` multi-targets `netstandard2.0;netstandard2.1;net8.0`. Because `tests/UnitTests/UnitTests.csproj` targets `netcoreapp3.1;net8.0`, running `dotnet test` only builds the `netstandard2.1` and `net8.0` targets of `PostHog` and hides this failure, while full-solution builds (`dotnet build --configuration Release` in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.github/workflows/main.yaml`) and `dotnet pack src/PostHog/PostHog.csproj` fail on `netstandard2.0`.

**Executed base vs. head comparison** (`.NET SDK 9.0.109`, Release):
```bash
dotnet build src/PostHog/PostHog.csproj -f netstandard2.0 --configuration Release --no-restore --nologo /p:GeneratePackageOnBuild=false
```
- Merge base (`17b0d4c0`): exit code `0` (`0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s)`).
- PR head (`bd41e090`): exit code `1`:
  - `src/PostHog/Features/LocalEvaluator.cs(1001,26): error CS0117: 'float' does not contain a definition for 'IsFinite'`
  - `src/PostHog/Features/LocalEvaluator.cs(1002,28): error CS0117: 'double' does not contain a definition for 'IsFinite'`

**Suggested fix:** Match the `netstandard2.0`-compatible checks already used in `NonFiniteSingleJsonConverter.cs:17`, `NonFiniteDoubleJsonConverter.cs:17`, and `PropertyFilterValue.cs:326,331`:
```csharp
static bool IsFinite(object value) => value switch
{
    float f => !float.IsNaN(f) && !float.IsInfinity(f),
    double d => !double.IsNaN(d) && !double.IsInfinity(d),
    _ => true
};
```
Consider verifying with `dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore --nologo` from the repository root so all target frameworks compile cleanly.

**Concern:** On `.NET Framework 4.x` (which consumes the `netstandard2.0` assembly), `overrideFloat.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` uses default `"G"` (`"G7"`, 7 significant digits) rather than shortest round-trip formatting, silently truncating 8–9 significant digit `float` overrides.

- **Governing contract:** On `.NET Core 3.0+` / `.NET 8+`, default `"G"` and `"R"` produce the same shortest round-trip string (verified on `.NET 9.0.8`: `0.1f` -> `"0.1"`, `BitIncrement(0.1f)` -> `"0.10000001"`, `10000001f` -> `"10000001"`). On `.NET Framework 4.x`, Microsoft's `Single.ToString` default `"G"` formats to 7 significant digits (`"G7"`).
- **Base vs. head & impact (`Test sketch (not executed)` — `.NET Framework 4.x` is unavailable on macOS arm64 and `netstandard2.0` does not currently compile due to `IsFinite`):**
  - `score > "0.1"` with `0.100000009f` (`MathF.BitIncrement(0.1f)`): `"G7"` formats as `"0.1"` -> inferred `false` (expected `true`; merge base's `StringifyFloatingPoint` at `PropertyFilterValue.cs:332` used `"R"` and returned `true`).
  - `score > "10000000"` with exact 24-bit integer `10000001f`: `"G7"` formats as `"1E+07"` -> inferred `false` (expected `true`; merge base returned `true`).
  - `score > "12345679"` with exact 24-bit integer `12345678f`: `"G7"` formats as `"1.234568E+07"` (`12345680`) -> inferred `true` (expected `false`; merge base returned `false`).
  - *(Note: on `.NET Framework 4.x`, `System.Text.Json`'s `net462`/`netstandard2.0` assembly uses `"G9"`, so `"G7"` loses precision relative to both exact numeric order and emitted JSON for 8–9 digit floats, whereas `"R"` preserves 8–9 digit precision on `.NET Framework 4.x` while still emitting `"0.1"` for `0.1f` across both `.NET Framework 4.x` and `.NET 8+`.)*
- **Reachability:** Affects `.NET Framework 4.x` hosts calling `EvaluateFlagsAsync` with boxed `float` person/group overrides having 8–9 significant digits near a threshold. Modern `.NET` (`net8.0`/`netstandard2.1`) is unaffected.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass `"R"` to match `StringifyFloatingPoint(float)` at `PropertyFilterValue.cs:332`:
  ```csharp
  float overrideFloat => doubleValue.CompareTo(double.Parse(overrideFloat.ToString("R", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)),
  ```
  Consider also adding `10000001f` (`gt "10000000"` -> `true`) and `12345678f` (`gt "12345679"` -> `false`) to the numeric boundary tests.

Thanks @dustinbyrne, both are in. `float`/`decimal` overrides are now compared via their JSON string value, and non-finite `float`/`double` overrides return false before the operator switch. The rows you asked for are in `LocalFeatureFlagsLoaderTests.VersionedDefinitionSnapshots.NumericOverridesResolveLocallyWithoutRemoteRequests`, going through `DefinitionsJson` + `EvaluateFlagsAsync` and asserting the flag is present, has no unresolved reason and no `/flags` request was made:

| override | rule | result |
|---|---|---|
| `0.1f` | `gt 0.1` / `lt 0.1` | false / false |
| `0.1f` | `lte 0.1` / `gte 0.1` | true / true |
| `BitIncrement(0.1f)` (control) | `gt 0.1` | true |
| `1.0000000000000003m` | `lt` / `gt 1.0000000000000004` | true / false |
| `NaN`, `-Inf` (float, double) | `lt`, `lte` | false |
| `NaN`, `+Inf` | `gte`, `gt` | false |
| `-1f` (control) | `lt 0` | true |

Red with the source from the previous commit: 20 failures; green: 0 failures (853 pass). `TheNumericBoundaryOverrides.Evaluate` now returns the tri-state result and uses `Assert.Equal(false/true, ...)`, so an inconclusive `null` no longer passes the negative cases.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks, both are in: the non-finite guard now uses `IsNaN`/`IsInfinity` and builds on `netstandard2.0` (Release build clean), and float overrides are formatted with `"R"`. Added the `10000001f` and `12345678f` rows. This comment was drafted with AI assistance.
